context:
Start from utils/version.py since it is the more clearly self-contained
fix (only needs a version string, not general benchbox internals). Decide
between importlib.metadata vs. a leaf benchbox/_version.py by checking
whether validate_version_consistency() needs anything else from the
package root; if not, importlib.metadata + tomllib fallback avoids adding
a new file. Apply the same fix to datagen_manifest.py once the pattern is
settled. Only then touch verbosity.py's guard and the __init__.py comment,
since removing them prematurely (before the cycle is actually broken) would
reintroduce the failure the guard exists to prevent.
description:
Architecture review (Work Area E, structural remediation) found that
`benchbox/utils/version.py:27` and `benchbox/utils/datagen_manifest.py:23`
both do `import benchbox` at module scope (to read `__version__` and to
resolve project-root paths, respectively). Because
`benchbox/utils/verbosity.py:12` imports `benchbox.utils.version`, and
effectively every subsystem imports `verbosity` for its logging mixin, this
single edge pulls a large strongly-connected component (~61 modules per the
review) into one cycle rooted at the package `__init__`.

Live symptoms already visible in the code, not just theory:

- `benchbox/__init__.py:14-16` carries a load-order comment: "`__version__`
  must be defined before `from . import platforms` because the platforms
  import chain can circle back to benchbox.cli.app which reads
  benchbox.__version__ at module level." That comment is a tell that the
  root module's initialization order is load-bearing.
- `benchbox/utils/verbosity.py:11-15` wraps its `benchbox.utils.version`
  import in `try/except ImportError` with the comment "optional dependency
  during bootstrapping" - a defensive guard that exists only because the
  cycle can make the import fail depending on where in package
  initialization it is triggered.

This is a structural-debt item independent of the shrink campaign:
`_project/goal-shrink-core-code.md` explicitly scopes god-class
decompositions and similar risk-trading refactors out of the autonomous
shrink loop. This TODO is a targeted import-layering fix, not a shrink-loop
item, and should not be picked up by that loop.

anti_patterns.dont: fold this into the shrink-campaign ledger
anti_patterns.why: _project/goal-shrink-core-code.md scopes structural/god-class-style refactors out of that loop; this is a standalone architecture fix.

anti_patterns.dont: remove the verbosity.py try/except ImportError guard before confirming w1+w2 actually eliminate the cycle
anti_patterns.why: removing it first will surface the exact ImportError the guard was added to suppress.

anti_patterns.dont: special-case version resolution per install method (editable vs wheel) with duplicated logic
anti_patterns.why: reuse the existing _PYPROJECT_CACHE/tomllib fallback for the source-tree case.

deferrals.reason: The review identified verbosity's fan-in as the multiplier, but a full SCC decomposition is a larger effort; this TODO targets the two root-importing leaf modules identified as the actual cycle cause. Re-scope separately if the cycle persists after this fix (see import-layering-enforcement, which adds tooling to detect any residual cycle).
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] superseded: import-layering-enforcement (DONE) shipped .importlinter with an active ratchet-down mechanism; residual cycle edges now handled incrementally by that tool, not a big-bang SCC breakup.
deferrals.summary: Broader breakup of the ~61-module SCC beyond the version/datagen_manifest edges

preserves.behavior: The lean-import guarantee already enforced by tests/unit/test_import_isolation.py (no heavy third-party modules like pandas/polars/pyarrow/duckdb on `import benchbox`) stays green.
The wheel's reported version (importlib.metadata / `benchbox --version` equivalent) stays correct for both editable/dev installs and built wheels.
validate_version_consistency() behavior in benchbox/__init__.py:30-46 (warns via UserWarning on RuntimeError, does not hard-fail import) is unchanged.

prior_art.concept: benchbox/utils/version.py:_PYPROJECT_CACHE and PROJECT_ROOT - existing tomllib-based pyproject parsing to reuse for the source-tree fallback rather than adding a second TOML reader.
tests/unit/test_import_isolation.py:_run_entrypoint - existing subprocess-isolation pattern to extend for the new w4 regression test, rather than inventing a new import-isolation harness.

verifications.description: Package still imports cleanly and lean-import isolation stays green

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/test_import_isolation.py -k version_no_root_import -v

Version consistency validation still runs at import time without hard-failing

work_units.notes:
Implemented via importlib.metadata.version("benchbox") with a
source-tree pyproject.toml fallback (used only on
PackageNotFoundError), NOT the leaf-module alternative. Reasoning:
get_package_version() must stay independently sourced from
get_pyproject_version() so check_version_consistency() can still
detect real drift between the two - test_check_version_consistency_detects_mismatch
monkeypatches only get_pyproject_version() and expects a mismatch to be
reported. If get_package_version() had unconditionally preferred the
source-tree pyproject.toml (as literally suggested in the TODO body for
the "editable/dev checkout" case), the two sources would have collapsed
into the same call, making that existing test always report
"consistent" - a real regression. importlib.metadata.version("benchbox")
currently returns "0.2.1", matching pyproject.toml exactly in this dev
checkout, so both tests
(test_check_version_consistency_matches_pyproject and
test_check_version_consistency_detects_mismatch) pass unmodified.
Did not add benchbox/_version.py - not needed once importlib.metadata
covers the installed/dev case, and it would have required updating
scripts/update_version.py's regex-based `__version__ = "..."` target in
benchbox/__init__.py, which is outside this TODO's scope_limit.
REVISED after review: the first cut mapped the "benchbox.__init__"
consistency source to get_package_version() (dist metadata), which
silently dropped coverage of the actual `__version__ = "..."` literal
in benchbox/__init__.py - the value scripts/update_version.py bumps at
release cut and the exact drift class that shipped the 0.3.0 wheel
with __version__ = "0.2.1". Fixed: added get_init_version() which
reads the literal STATICALLY from the benchbox/__init__.py source file
(same regex scripts/update_version.py uses; works inside wheels since
__init__.py ships; no package-root import, so the cycle stays broken)
and mapped the "benchbox.__init__" source to it. Dist metadata is now
checked as its own distinct "installed-dist" source (absent-when-not-
installed is exempt from missing-source accounting in both dev and
installed modes - a bare checkout is legitimate - but participates in
mismatch detection when present). get_package_version() remains
importlib.metadata-first (fallback: init literal, then pyproject).
Added four tests to tests/unit/utils/test_utils_version_management.py
covering the static read, init-literal drift, installed-dist drift,
and missing-installed-dist tolerance.

work_units.notes:
Deviated from the literal "assert benchbox.platforms/deep submodule
absent from sys.modules" wording: Python's import machinery always
fully initializes a parent package before importing any dotted
submodule, so a subprocess doing `import benchbox.utils.version` alone
can never observe "benchbox not fully initialized" - that part of the
original test proposal is not achievable given CPython import
semantics, regardless of this fix. Implemented instead as an AST-based
static check (test_version_no_root_import, parametrized over both
files) asserting neither utils/version.py nor
utils/datagen_manifest.py contains a module-level `import benchbox`
statement - the actual, checkable claim that was broken before and
fixed by w1/w2. Added in tests/unit/test_import_isolation.py per the
prior_art pointer (reused _run_entrypoint, generalized with an optional
heavy_roots param for the separate NYCTaxi test in w5).
work_units.summary: Add a regression test asserting utils.version does not import the package root

REVISED after review: making NYCTaxi lazy exposed an import-order
hazard in tests/unit/cli/test_benchmark_hooks.py - its per-test
registry snapshot/restore fixture wipes registrations performed by
module imports that first happen INSIDE a test body, and sys.modules
caching prevents re-registration, so
TestRealBenchmarkSpecs::test_nyctaxi_taxi_types_parser went red
(KeyError 'taxi_types') once `import benchbox` stopped guaranteeing
nyctaxi's registration. Fixed by adding a module-scoped autouse
fixture in that test file importing all five benchmark modules whose
specs the file reads (nyctaxi, tsbs_devops, tpch_skew, vector_search,
joinorder - the latter two were always lazy and carried the same
latent hazard) before the first per-test snapshot is taken. Grepped
tests/ for other list_option_specs/_option_specs consumers: no other
file combines snapshot/restore with in-test registration imports, and
all pass in isolation with -n 0.
